title: Rotation retro: stability digest and handoff notes (Jul 21 2028)
content:
Summary:

Mid-rotation digest covering: a P2 latency/429 spike (Jul 19), small regional failover test on Jul 20, SLO consumption trends, runbook tweaks, and handoff notes for the next rotation. Focus: reduce repeat prefix-cache invalidations and stabilize autoscaler hysteresis.

Incidents (concise):

1) P2: increased 429s and token latency spike — Jul 19 04:12-04:45 UTC
- Impact: ~7% increase in 429 responses for hosted-api write path (model generate) in us-west-2; 95th token latency rose from 180ms to 470ms for 60s windows.
- Root cause (prelim): concurrent rollback of kernel-selector PR (runtime PR #4432) triggered a short-lived mismatch between kernel selection table and prefix/KV cache eviction timings. During the rollback we saw increased KV-cache misses and a regression in batching behavior that bubbled into higher queueing latency and backpressure (429s).
- Mitigation: manual rollback completed to a safe commit and TTL for KV-prefix cache was temporarily increased; autoscaler aggressive cooldown disabled for 15 minutes to allow queue drain.
- Owner: Ethan Walker
- Follow-up tickets: SRE-2478 (investigate kernel-selector rollback safeguards), SRE-2499 (add canary for prefix-cache invalidation paths).

2) Smoke regional failover - planned test — Jul 20 01:00 UTC
- Purpose: verify cross-region fallback policy for critical model routes under degraded capacity.
- Observations: automatic fallback to eu-west-1 worked as configured for 3 of 4 routes; route /v1/chat/model-x misrouted due to stale routing policy in edge-config (edge-config drift).
- Action: updated edge-config sync job to run every 3m (was 10m) and added a check in rollout pipeline to validate route table freshness.
- Owner: Nina Morales

SLOs & Metrics snapshot (WTD, week-to-date ending Jul 21):

- Availability SLO (hosted inference ingest): target 99.95%
  - Current WTD: 99.91% -> error budget used: ~8%
- Token latency SLO (tail): target p99 <= 250ms
  - Current WTD: p99 = 312ms (spike concentrated Jul 19 incident) -> trending up, risk if similar regressions occur.
- 429/5xx budget: 429s spiked to 7% in affected region during incident; overall 429 rate WTD: 0.85% (target <0.5%) -> budget consumption noted.

Runbook & playbook changes proposed:

- Prefix-cache invalidation playbook (new): add a staged invalidation procedure (canary prefix->region->global) with automated rollback if 429 > 0.5% during canary window. Owner: Jonas Becker. Due: 2028-07-28.
- Kernel-selector rollback safe-guard: create a pre-rollback validation that runs a synthetic generation workload with sample token distribution and validates KV hit-rate and batching latency. Patch in runtime repo: PR 4432 follow-up. Owner: Ethan. Due: 2028-07-25.
- Autoscaler hysteresis tuning: increase cooldown on scale-down by 40s for model-serving pools with median sequence length > 512. Owner: SRE infra. Due: 2028-07-26.
- Edge-config sync job: reduce interval to 3m and add CI gate check in rollout pipeline. Owner: Nina. Done: Jul 21.

On-call handoff (for next rotation starting Jul 22 08:00 UTC):

- Current risk areas to watch:
  - Kernel-selector rollout activity: pause all non-urgent kernel changes until follow-up validations are in-place.
  - KV-prefix cache churn: watch KV hit-rate dashboards and alert thresholds for >10% drop over 10m.
  - Autoscaling flaps: monitor scale-down/scale-up churn (metric: consecutive scale events >3 in 15m).

- Suggested watchlist for first 4 hours:
  1) p99 token latency (global + us-west-2)
  2) KV cache hit-rate (per-model, per-region)
  3) 429 spike rate per route
  4) Autoscaler event rate for dedicated pools

- Immediate contacts if incident escalates:
  - On-call SRE: rotation primary (pager) — see pager schedule for name
  - Runtime owner: Ethan Walker (pager + mobile)
  - Platform infra: Jonas Becker
  - Product lead for hosted-api: Maya Chen (for customer comms)

Action items (with owners and expected status):

- SRE-2478: Deep-dive on kernel-selector rollback mechanics and create pre-rollback synthetic validation — Owner: Ethan Walker — ETA 2028-07-25 (in_progress).
- SRE-2499: Canary invalidation playbook + automated rollback triggers — Owner: Jonas Becker — ETA 2028-07-28 (todo).
- UPDATE-EDGE: CI gate for edge-config freshness + reduced sync interval (3m) — Owner: Nina Morales — status: done (2028-07-21).
- AUTOSCALE-TUNE: Implement scale-down cooldown change for long-sequence pools — Owner: eng-sre-infra — ETA 2028-07-26 (in_progress).
- COMM-DRILL: Run a customer-facing outage drill for Reserved/Dedicated customers to validate SLA comms runbook — Owner: Maya Chen — ETA 2028-08-02 (todo).

Meeting notes / decisions from rotation retro (Jul 21 sync):

- Decision: introduce a mandatory synthetic KV-hit-rate check in any runtime kernel rollout (agreed unanimous).
- Decision: reduce edge-config sync interval; treat route-table drift as a P1 if it affects region fallback during tests.
- Next retro: Jul 28 — focus on canary invalidation playbook and autoscaler tuning results.

Open questions / blockers:

- Should we adopt a rolling canary that pins a small percentage of traffic to the new kernel-selection commit for 10 minutes and run offline validators concurrently? (pros and cons debated; solution is the staged invalidation playbook).
- Do we need a separate alert channel for prefix-cache health (separate from general cache dashboards)? Proposal: yes, create dedicated alerts and a Slack channel #cache-health.

Appendix / quick diagnostics (links):

- Incident timeline and raw logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/query?range=2028-07-19T04:00Z-2028-07-19T05:00Z&query=kernel-selector%20rollback
- KV hit-rate dashboard (us-west-2): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv-hitrate/us-west-2
- Token-latency p99 trend: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/token-latency/p99
- Follow-up PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4432
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-2478

Notes to next on-call: keep calm, follow playbooks, and call out any repeat pattern (cache miss -> batching shift -> latency -> 429) as early as possible. If in doubt, escalate to runtime owner and spin a bridge early (we lost ground during the Jul 19 rollback because the bridge was created later than ideal).

-- Priya

(quick checklist for handoff read: top-level summary, incident list, action items with owners, watchlist metrics, immediate contacts)
